newsitem.title: USA: Sears names Salter home stores president.
newsitem.headline: Sears names Salter home stores president.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Thursday it named William Salter as president of home stores, succeeding Marvin Stern, 60, who becomes a special advisor to Sears Chairman Arthur Martinez.

In his new position, Salter, who had been president of hardlines, assumes responsibility for all Sears off-the-mall formats selling home-related merchandise, including Sears Hardware, HomeLife Furniture and Sears dealer stores.
Salter, 53, joined the company in 1965 as a merchandise manager.
Sears said the appointments of Salter and Stern are part of its strategy for continued development of its full-line department stores and accelerated growth of its off-the-mall stores.
In a realignment of responsibilities within full-line stores, Sears said Robert Mettler, president-apparel and home fashions, was promoted to the newly created position of president-merchandising.
In this position, Mettler will be responsible for all merchandise buying, product development, strategy and marketing in Sears full-line stores.
Mettler, 56, joined Sears as president-apparel and home fashions group in 1993.

Allan Stewart continues as president-stores, responsible for store planning, construction and licensed businesses. He also assumes responsibility for human resources and finance within the full-line store organization. Stewart, 54, was appointed to his current position in 1993.
Salter, Mettler and Stewart will continue to report to Martinez.
"Today's appointments demonstrate the depth of our management team and our commitment to aggressively grow our full-line and off-the-mall stores," Martinez said in a statement.
Sears has more than 800 full-line department stores and 1,500 off-the-mall stores.
